The order is posted from `postOrder` in the chart's common library to `POST {restBaseUrl}/order`. The webservices REST module's `OrderResource` `save` passes it to `OrderService.saveOrder`, which ends in `OrderDAO.saveOrder` and a Hibernate `saveOrUpdate`.

1. **Frontend request:** `postOrder` in `openmrs-esm-patient-chart/packages/esm-patient-common-lib/src/orders/postOrders.ts` (lines 202-209) sends the POST via `openmrsFetch` to `${restBaseUrl}/order`. Its caller `postOrders` (lines 157-200) calls it per order at line 182. `postOrdersOnNewEncounter` (line 63) is the entry point when a new encounter is also created. I did not read past its first line, so its end line is unverified.
2. **Server REST handler:** `OrderResource1_10.save` (lines 326-329) overrides `OrderResource1_8.save` (lines 72-75) and calls `Context.getOrderService().saveOrder(delegate, null)`. `OrderResource2_2` extends `OrderResource1_10`, so the 1_10 override applies to current servers. I did not find the generic REST controller that routes `POST /order` into `save`; that link is unverified.
3. **Core service:** `OrderServiceImpl.saveOrder` (lines 114-117) delegates to the private `saveOrder` (lines 165-379), which validates the order and then calls `dao.saveOrder(order)` at line 378. The interface declaration is `OrderService.saveOrder` (line 135).
4. **Data access:** `HibernateOrderDAO.saveOrder` (lines 92-95) calls `HibernateUtil.saveOrUpdate` on the current Hibernate session. The interface is `OrderDAO.saveOrder` (line 47).
